toy_inyourarea.title: Rochdale Christmas Toy Appeal aims to deliver 10,000 gifts to children in need
toy_inyourarea.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council's Christmas Toy Appeal seeks donations to provide gifts for 3,000 children living in poverty this festive season.
toy_inyourarea.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has launched its Christmas Toy Appeal, aiming to deliver 10,000 new, unwrapped gifts to 3,000 children living in poverty this festive season.

The appeal, which has been running for 13 years, encourages residents to donate toys to help ensure that no child goes without a present this Christmas.

Donations can be made at various collection points across the borough, including The Trade Centre UK and The Old Police Station. All contributions, regardless of size, are welcomed, with postal deliveries required by 11 December.

The Christmas Toy Appeal has been providing festive cheer to local families since 2013, helping to alleviate some of the pressures faced by those in need during the holiday season.

The council's charity is coordinating the initiative, which has become a vital resource for families in the area.

Residents are encouraged to participate in the appeal to help spread joy and support children in their community. For those wishing to donate, collection points are available throughout Rochdale, and all gifts must be new and unwrapped.

toy_editor.title: Rochdale Council launches Christmas Toy Appeal for local children in need
toy_editor.excerpt: The Christmas Toy Appeal aims to support local children living in poverty by collecting donations until 11 December.
toy_editor.content_html:
Rochdale Council has launched its Christmas Toy Appeal to support local children living in poverty, with donations accepted until Friday 11 December.

The appeal, organised by the charity Number One Riverside Giving Back, aims to provide gifts to children who may otherwise go without this Christmas due to financial pressures faced by their families.

Helen Walton, a council policy advisor from the charity, expressed gratitude for the community's support, stating that every donation is important for the appeal's success and that requests for help have already been received this year.

This initiative is part of a broader effort to alleviate the impact of poverty during the holidays and ensure that children have presents on Christmas Day.

toy_council.title: Rochdale Christmas Toy Appeal seeks donations to support local children
toy_council.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council is calling for donations for its Christmas Toy Appeal, which helps local children in need. Donations are accepted until 11 December 2026.
toy_council.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has launched its Christmas Toy Appeal, urging residents to donate toys for local children living in poverty. The appeal, which has been running annually since 2013, aims to ensure that children have something to unwrap on Christmas morning.

Donations for the appeal can be made until 11 December 2026, at various local libraries and leisure centres across the borough.

Last year, the appeal distributed a record 10,000 toys, highlighting the community's generosity and the increasing need for support among families facing financial pressures during the festive season.

The appeal is organised by the 'Number One Riverside Giving Back' charity, which has been instrumental in coordinating efforts to provide festive cheer to children in need.

The council's initiative is a response to the growing number of requests for help from families, making it crucial for many during the holiday season.

Residents are encouraged to contribute to the appeal, which has been supported by the kindness of the local community. Last year, Holy Trinity CE School collected gifts for the initiative, showcasing the collaborative spirit of the borough.

Rochdale Borough Council Christmas Toy Appeal: www.rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/696/christmas-toy-appeal-calls-on-borough-residents-to-help-families-in-need

toy_roundup_editor.title: Christmas giving in Rochdale: the toy appeal, the foodbank and the mayor's charities
toy_roundup_editor.excerpt: New, unwrapped toys for children aged up to 16 are needed by Friday 11 December, while Rochdale Foodbank is short of juice, rice, toothpaste and coffee.
toy_roundup_editor.content_html:
Rochdale borough residents wanting to give this Christmas can help children living in poverty, families relying on food parcels, and the five charities chosen by the mayor.

The borough's Christmas Toy Appeal is collecting gifts until Friday 11 December, so local children living in poverty have a present to open on Christmas Day.

Gifts must be new, not wrapped, and suitable for children up to 16. Organisers say presents for babies and teenagers are especially welcome, because those age groups receive fewer donations.

Gifts can be left during opening hours at any borough library and at venues including Rochdale Leisure Centre, the Crown Oil Arena, Middleton Arena, Heywood Sports Village and Littleborough Sports Centre. They can also be posted to Number One Riverside Giving Back – Christmas Toy Appeal, Number One Riverside, Smith Street, Rochdale OL16 1XU.

The appeal is run by the Number One Riverside Giving Back charity with Rochdale Borough Council, Rochdale AFC, Your Trust and Rochdale Town Centre Management. More than 10,000 toys were donated in 2024, and more than 57,000 since the appeal began in 2014.

Rochdale Foodbank fed 8,444 adults and 4,556 children in 2025, up 13% and 8% on 2024.

Its current shortages are fruit juice, rice, toothpaste, shampoo, treats and coffee. It also lists long-life milk, jam, pasta sauces, tinned fruit, tinned potatoes, sugar, tea bags and cereal as urgent.

Food can be dropped at the warehouse on Newgate, Rochdale, between 10am and midday, Monday to Friday, or at collection points in Tesco on Silk Street, Asda on Dane Street and Morrisons on Kingsway. Money can be given through the foodbank's JustGiving page.

The Mayor of Rochdale, Councillor Faisal Rana, is raising money this year for Springhill Hospice, The Christie, Sands, Rochdale Veterans' Breakfast Club and Rochdale Women's Welfare Association.

Shoppers can support them at no extra cost by signing up to the Easy Fundraising app, where participating brands donate a share of online purchases. Donations can also be arranged through the Mayor's Office on 01706 924796 or mayoral@rochdale.gov.uk.

Sources: Rochdale Borough Council; Rochdale Foodbank. Photograph: Rochdale Daily library.

church_service.title: St Luke’s Church in Deeplish to hold Remembrance Day service on 8 November
church_service.excerpt: St Luke’s Church in Deeplish will hold a Remembrance Day service of Holy Communion on 8 November, officiated by Revd Natty Gray, followed by community refreshments.
church_service.content_html:
St Luke’s Church in Deeplish is set to hold a Remembrance Day service of Holy Communion on 8 November at 10.30am, officiated by Revd Natty Gray.

This service will include readings from 1 Thessalonians 4: 13-end and Matthew 25: 1-13, providing a moment for reflection and remembrance.

Following the service, attendees are invited to enjoy tea or coffee and engage in conversation, fostering community spirit among regular members and newcomers alike. This gathering will provide an opportunity for attendees to connect and share their thoughts on the significance of Remembrance Day.

In addition to the Remembrance Day service, St Luke’s Church will host a Bible Study on 11 November at 10am, welcoming anyone interested in exploring the Bible in an informal setting.

Later that day, a Morning Praise service will take place at 11am, led by Reader Sue Horobin, featuring readings from Daniel 5: 13-30 and Revelation 7: 1-4,9-17.

The church is also selling some of its youth group costumes, which have taken up considerable space.

church_notices.title: St Luke’s Church in Deeplish announces upcoming services and community events
church_notices.excerpt: St Luke’s Church in Deeplish will hold a Morning Praise service on November 1, followed by a series of community activities throughout the month.
church_notices.content_html:
St Luke’s Church in Deeplish is set to hold a service of Morning Praise on November 1 at 10am, officiated by Reader Sue Horobin. This service will be followed by tea and coffee, providing an opportunity for attendees to socialise and connect with one another.

On 4 November, the church will host a Bible Study at 10am, followed by another Morning Praise service at 11am, officiated by Revd Natty Gray. The church welcomes both regular members and newcomers to join their friendly congregation.

Last Sunday, the church celebrated Holy Communion, officiated by Revd Ian Butterworth, and will continue with communion next week, led by Kirsten Rutherford. After each service, refreshments will be available, allowing for fellowship among attendees.

In addition to the services, the church is selling some of its youth group costumes, which have attracted interest from societies worldwide, including buyers from Germany, Italy, Norway, and America.

sleepout_bot.title: Rochdale Sleep Out raises funds for homeless support
sleepout_bot.excerpt: Fundraisers gathered at Crown Oil Arena for the annual Sleep Out, raising awareness and funds for homelessness initiatives in the community.
sleepout_bot.content_html:
Fundraisers spent a night outdoors at Rochdale's Crown Oil Arena to raise awareness and vital funds for people experiencing homelessness. This event, the second annual Sleep Out organised by Petrus Communities and RAFC Community Trust, saw supporters from across the borough come together for a common cause.

The money raised will support the Changing Lives initiative, a football programme designed to assist individuals facing homelessness or living in supported accommodation.

The initiative aims to enhance participants' mental health, physical well-being, and social inclusion through free football sessions, while also providing personal development opportunities, including pathways into volunteering, education, and employment.

Louise Scriven, Fundraising and Partnerships Coordinator at Petrus, emphasised that the Sleep Out is not about pretending to experience homelessness, but about standing in solidarity with those facing housing insecurities. She noted that last year's event significantly impacted participants, helping them rebuild confidence, forge new friendships, and develop skills to become active community members.

The funds raised from this year's Sleep Out will continue to provide essential accommodation, support, advice, and opportunities for those experiencing homelessness and disadvantage in Rochdale, Oldham, and Burnley.

Donations are crucial for sustaining these services and making a difference in the lives of vulnerable individuals in the community.

sleepout_editor.title: Rochdale Sleep Out raises almost £10,000 as organisers make final appeal
sleepout_editor.excerpt: Supporters spent the night outdoors at the Crown Oil Arena for Petrus Community and Rochdale AFC Community Trust, with the annual charity Sleep Out now close to its £10,000 fundraising milestone.
sleepout_editor.content_html:
Supporters from across Rochdale spent Friday night outdoors in solidarity with people experiencing homelessness, helping an annual charity Sleep Out raise almost £10,000.

The event, organised by Petrus Community and Rochdale AFC Community Trust, took place on Friday 9 October at the Crown Oil Arena. Participants were joined in the fundraising effort by donors and local businesses.

Petrus said the total was now approaching the £10,000 milestone and appealed for one final push to reach it. The figure is a provisional amount reported by the organisers, rather than a confirmed final total.

The Sleep Out aimed to raise awareness of housing insecurity and homelessness while giving participants a limited insight into the practical challenges of spending a night without a comfortable bed. Organisers stressed that taking part for one night cannot replicate the uncertainty and difficulties faced by people who have no safe place to call home.

Money raised will help sustain vital support for people experiencing homelessness and disadvantage. Petrus provides accommodation, housing advice, outreach, wellbeing support and opportunities to help people rebuild stability across Rochdale, Oldham and Burnley.

The partnership between Petrus and Rochdale AFC Community Trust also supports the Changing Lives programme, which uses football, wellbeing activities and pathways into education, volunteering and employment to help people experiencing homelessness or living in supported accommodation.

Last year's Sleep Out raised £7,875.52 for the two organisations. This year's organisers have thanked everyone who slept outdoors, donated or helped make the event possible.

Petrus is encouraging Rochdale residents who wish to support the final fundraising push to donate through its official website: https://www.petrus.org.uk/.
sleepout_editor.source_name: Petrus Community / Rochdale AFC Community Trust

contract_1.title: Rochdale Borough Council awards contract for Empty Homes Leasing Programme
contract_1.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has awarded a contract to CAREPOINT HC LIMITED for the GM Empty Homes TA Leasing Programme, aimed at providing temporary accommodation for families.
contract_1.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has awarded a contract to CAREPOINT HC LIMITED for the GM Empty Homes Temporary Accommodation (TA) Leasing Programme. This framework contract is set for an initial term of four years or until the contract value reaches £3.5 million, whichever comes first.

The programme aims to lease or acquire 2-4 bedroom homes to provide temporary accommodation for families that the Council has a duty to support under sections 188, 190, or 193 of the Housing Act.

The initiative seeks to incentivise property owners with homes that have been empty for six months or more to bring them back into use, thereby reducing the costs associated with temporary accommodation.

In addition to the framework contract, a call-off contract has also been awarded to CAREPOINT HC LIMITED for a minimum of 20 to a maximum of 32 properties. The value of this call-off contract is not guaranteed, reflecting the flexible nature of the agreement.

This initiative is significant for Rochdale as it addresses the pressing need for safe and secure accommodation for families facing housing challenges. By utilising empty homes, the Council aims to improve housing availability while managing costs effectively.

contract_2.title: Rochdale Borough Council awards contract for new income management system
contract_2.excerpt: Civica UK Limited has been awarded a contract by Rochdale Borough Council for an income management system to enhance payment processing.
contract_2.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has awarded a contract to Civica UK Limited for a new Income Management System, aimed at improving the efficiency of cash receipting, e-payments, and overall income management.

The software will be used for the receipt, reconciliation, and reporting of payments made to the council for various services provided to customers and charge payers.

This development is significant for the council as it seeks to streamline its financial operations, ensuring better management of public funds and improved service delivery to residents.

The implementation of this system is expected to enhance the council's ability to manage income effectively, benefiting both the council and its service users.
